report:
ENGINE FINDINGS (globe + question engine). Measured with a temporary jest probe (since deleted) on generated contacts and the six sample networks. Repo untouched.

1. WHAT THE PAGE CAN ASK OF THE GLOBE TODAY (NetworkGraph props, src/components/network/NetworkGraph.js:208)
- atlas: the whole layout. The page rebuilds it on every filter change (network.js:663, buildAtlas(visibleContacts, {groupBy})).
- focus {id, nonce}: fly to one node (root, group, company, person's parent). A new nonce means fly again. An unknown id falls back to the root.
- viewId: dims everything outside that cluster (inFocus). The globe reports the cluster in view through onViewNode.
- highlightIds: a Set of person ids (p:<dedupeKey>). Lit people and their parent containers stay bright, and the camera turns to their centroid. If they are spread more than 1.1 rad apart it only faces that direction at home zoom, which looks like nothing happened.
- selectedId: draws a pulse along the branch from root to the node.
- There is no lens prop. A lens is a contact filter in the page (visibleContacts), so it triggers a full rebuild.
- Node ids follow the path (g/role:founders/industry:Big Tech/c:google). Only person ids are stable across groupings and filters.

2. FILTERING = NEW LAYOUT
When a lens, source, company or direct-only filter is applied, the atlas is repacked and wrapGlobe re-places the clusters: the largest faces the viewer and the rest go wherever they fit. Every cluster moves, and the camera flies 750 ms to the focus id or to the root. The "same contacts, same place" promise holds only while the filter stays the same. A highlight does not rebuild the atlas, so it keeps everyone in place. That makes it the right tool for presets and answers.

3. ONE COMPANY SPLIT ACROSS GROUPS
In the default role grouping (role > industry > company), many companies are split into several nodes:
- vc-investor: 54 of 255 companies split. Stripe is 10+11+1 and Google is 12+7.
- founder-operator: 44 of 213. Google is 17+24.
- sales-crm: 58 of 147. Marlowe is spread over 8 nodes (1+1+1+2+7+2+3+1).
- healthcare: 28 of 97.
"Largest company" (network.js:740) picks the single biggest company node, so on the VC file it flies to a Google slice of 12 while Stripe has 22 people in all. The code does fly; "does nothing" was not reproduced here. Likely causes:
- the camera is already near that slice;
- the whole file has one company per node;
- for an X import with no companies, biggest is null and the button is hidden;
- the "By company" grouping freezes the page (see 4).
Ways to treat a company as one unit:
- (a) Compute the largest company from groupByCompany(visibleContacts) (correct totals) and light all its people with highlightIds. This works today with no layout change; the panel then shows the full 22.
- (b) Have buildAtlas add a companyKey -> [node ids] index (cheap) so the page can count, label and fly to every slice.
- (c) The existing companyFilter rebuilds the globe for just that company.
- (d) groupBy=company has one node per company but is unusable (see 4).

4. COST OF REBUILDING
buildAtlas (role grouping, generated contacts, cold caches):
- 500 contacts: 31 ms
- 5,000: 57-88 ms (7,415 nodes)
- 30,000: 278 ms (44,420 nodes)
Warm rebuild: 3 / 22 / 133 ms. Industry grouping: 3 / 21 / 125 ms. A filtered subset (raise lens, 3,685 of 30k): 13 ms.
Globe placement (wrapOntoGlobe) is 3-14 ms when there are a few top clusters.
SEVERE: with groupBy=company there are hundreds of top clusters, and placement is O(attempts × tops² × 700 spots):
- generated 500 contacts (140 companies): 6.5 s
- small sample (14 companies): 21 ms
- lp-fundraising (80): 1.9 s
- healthcare (97): 3.3 s
- sales-crm (147): 10.5 s
- founder-operator (213): 17.8 s
- vc-investor (255): 31.6 s
5,000 and 30,000 contacts were not run. Extrapolated, they would take minutes to hours. This freezes the main thread. Fix it by capping the top clusters (the way MAX_HUBS=16 does for industry and country, folding the tail into "Other companies") or by cheaper placement. Canvas drawing time was not measured.

5. QUESTION ENGINE (src/server/network/query.js; API src/pages/api/network/query.js)
The rules handle these question types:
- company, "who-at": "know/people/works at X", several companies joined by or/and/commas;
- intro path: intro/path/route to X. Direct contacts, plus people at X's investors from the public company profile. Past employees are always [];
- 17 role groups, by regex on the title;
- 14 keyword sectors (KEYWORD_GROUPS) matched in title, company and tags;
- location: a capitalised place after "in/near", a short alias (sf, nyc...), or a lower-case place present in the data;
- lens: raise / source / diligence.
All categories must match (AND); keywords are ORed. When the rules find nothing specific, the question text alone goes to the model. The model's filter has the same shape, with no date or tag field.
The response contains: question, filters{companies, roles, keywords, locations, intent, lens}, parsedBy, intent, contactCount, results (up to 100 of {contact{key,name,company,position,location,profileUrl,connectedOn,source}, score, reasons[], companyMatch, role, roleLabel}), total, possiblyRelated{results,total} for company questions, intro{direct, possiblyRelated, viaInvestors[{investor,evidence,contacts,total}], investorsChecked, profileStatus, notes}, notes, contactsFrom.

6. CONTENT-BUILT PRESETS, TRIED ON THE SAMPLES (rules only)
- "Who do I know at <largest company>": works everywhere and gives the exact totals (Stripe 22, Google 41, MGH 22, Marlowe 18, CalPERS 5, Bluebird 6). The fixed example "Who do I know at Google?" returns 0 on healthcare, LP and sales.
- "Intro paths to <#2 company>": returns the direct people. There are no investor paths for non-startups (Google, Johns Hopkins, a pension plan), only a note.
- "<top industry> founders": BROKEN. The map's industry labels (Big Tech, Software, Investing, Finance & operations, Venture capital, Industrials) are not query keywords and are silently dropped. "Big Tech founders" returns all 44 founders. Labels that are keywords match by title and company words, not by industryOf: "Healthcare founders" gives 0 on sales-crm although the map shows 115 Healthcare, and "Venture capital founders" gives 0 on the VC file.
- "People I connected with this year" / "in 2026": CANNOT. There is no date filter; it gives 0 on every LinkedIn file, even though connectedOn is present for 544/544 (VC) and 83 connected in 2026. On the LP file, "2026" only hit because a tag reads "met 2026".
- "Everyone tagged <tag>": works by accident through the word fallback (prospect 107, "met 2026" 23). Keywords are ORed and also match titles and company names, so a tag like "partner" (69 in sales-crm) would also pull in every Partner by title. There is no tag filter.
- "People in <city>": works where a location exists (Austin 27, Seattle 14, New York 63, lower case too). LinkedIn and X exports have none.
- "Senior people at my largest company": not understood (word fallback, junk results).
- "Partners at venture firms": "venture firms" is parsed as a company, giving 0.
- Lens counts filter almost nothing: source matches 499/544 (VC), 444/451 (founder) and 232/328 (sales).
- In sales-crm, 69 contacts count as "investors" and "raise" returns a "Buyer" as an investor, so the VC vocabulary misreads a sales CRM.
- The healthcare file has raise=0.
facts: The globe accepts focus{id,nonce}, viewId, highlightIds (a Set of p:<dedupeKey> ids) and selectedId; it has no lens prop, so lenses and filters go through a full atlas rebuild, while highlightIds lights people without moving anything and is the right channel for presets and answers.

Any contact filter repacks and re-places every cluster on the globe (the largest faces the viewer) and flies 750 ms to the focus or the root; node ids follow the path (e.g. g/role:founders/industry:Big Tech/c:google), so only person ids are stable across groupings and filters.

In the default role grouping companies are split into several nodes (Stripe 10+11+1 and Google 12+7 on the VC sample; 54 of 255 companies split; Marlowe in 8 nodes in sales-crm), so 'Largest company' (network.js:740) flies to one slice (Google 12) rather than the true largest (Stripe 22).

To treat a company as one unit, compute it from groupByCompany(visibleContacts) and light all its people via highlightIds, or have buildAtlas add a companyKey -> node ids index; both are cheap and keep the layout.
buildAtlas costs about 31 ms / 57-88 ms / 278 ms for 500 / 5,000 / 30,000 generated contacts (133 ms warm at 30k, 44,420 nodes); globe placement takes 3-14 ms when there are a few top groups.

Grouping 'By company' freezes the main thread: globe placement is O(attempts x tops^2 x 700) and took 31.6 s on the 544-person VC sample, 17.8 s on founder-operator and 10.5 s on sales-crm; it needs a cap on top clusters like MAX_HUBS=16.

The query rules recognise companies, intro paths, 17 role groups, 14 sector keywords, locations and three lenses (raise/source/diligence); categories AND together, keywords OR; only the question text goes to the model, and only when the rules find nothing specific; results carry contact.key, reasons, companyMatch, total, possiblyRelated and intro.

There is no date or tag filter: 'people I connected with this year' returns 0 on every LinkedIn sample, although all rows carry connectedOn (83 of 544 in 2026); a tag query works only through the word fallback, which also matches titles (tag 'partner' vs title Partner).

The industry labels on the map (Big Tech, Software, Investing, Venture capital...) are not query keywords: 'Big Tech founders' returns all 44 founders, and 'Healthcare founders' gives 0 on sales-crm although the map shows 115 Healthcare, so presets built from map labels must filter on industryOf on the client, not through the query engine.

The fixed lenses and examples do not fit most networks: Source matches 499/544, 444/451 and 232/328 contacts; healthcare has raise=0; sales-crm counts 69 'investors' (a 'Buyer' as investor); 'Who do I know at Google?' returns 0 on the healthcare, LP and sales samples; LinkedIn and X exports have no location, so city presets apply only to CSV and CRM uploads.
